encounters.cc: Acute onset of blurry vision with intermittent flashes of light and new floaters in the right eye for the past 10 hours.

lines: Acute onset of blurry vision with intermittent flashes of light and new floaters in the right eye for the past 10 hours.

This 69-year-old female with long-standing Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Alzheimer's disease diagnosed in 2020, and recent evaluation for adult physical abuse presents to the Emergency Department with acute visual symptoms.
She describes the vision loss as blurry with intermittent flashes of light and new-onset floaters, and states that she first noticed the symptoms after walking outside on a windy day.
She denies trauma, eye rubbing, or recent ocular procedures.
She reports no eye redness or discharge, but notes mild aching in the affected eye.

encounters.cc: Decline in functional status with desire to discontinue all medications including chemotherapy, antihypertensives, and diabetes drugs.

lines: Decline in functional status with desire to discontinue all medications including chemotherapy, antihypertensives, and diabetes drugs.
The patient with Alzheimer's disease and metastatic breast cancer returns to the Palliative Care clinic with functional decline, having previously presented with memory loss and unexplained bruising.
She has been on multiple lines of chemotherapy, with the last regimen discontinued 2 months ago due to disease progression and significant side effects.
The patient expresses a desire to stop all her medications, including her oral anti-hypertensives and diabetes management drugs.
She also states that she no longer wishes to eat or drink, explaining that she accepts her impending death and prefers to die naturally without further medical intervention.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue requiring admission for anemia workup; on hospital day 2, developed acute shortness of breath and chest heaviness one hour after completing transfusion of two units packed red blood cells.

lines: Progressive fatigue requiring admission for anemia workup; on hospital day 2, developed acute shortness of breath and chest heaviness one hour after completing transfusion of two units packed red blood cells.
The patient is a 70-year-old with metastatic breast cancer admitted for progressive anemia, following recent palliative care evaluation and emergency department treatment for hypercalcemia.
On hospital day 2, she receives two units of packed red blood cells for persistent anemia.
One hour after the transfusion is completed, she develops shortness of breath and a sensation of chest heaviness.
There is no rash, no fever, no hypotension, and no hemoglobinuria.
